title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Friday's close capped a five-day win streak — S&P 500 +0.59% to 7,811.54, Nasdaq +0.64% to 27,366.17, Dow +423pts (0.83%) to 51,654.95 — even as long-dated Treasury yields sat at fresh 24-year highs; no US trading over the weekend.

Companies: Q3 bank earnings season kicks off Tuesday with JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, BlackRock, Wells Fargo and Citigroup reporting, followed by TSMC's results Thursday (Oct 15) and P&G's virtual annual meeting Tuesday.
Macro/Policy: All eyes on Wednesday's September CPI (8:30am ET) and Thursday's PPI — the last major inflation readings before the Fed's Oct 28 FOMC meeting.

Macro/Policy: Trump formed a White House committee to investigate Fed Governor Lisa Cook over mortgage-fraud allegations; a closed-door hearing is set for Nov 5, adding to pressure on Fed independence, while Cook's lawyers dispute the process's legitimacy.
Macro/Policy: IEA's October Oil Market Report is due Wednesday, a fresh read on global supply/demand balances after recent Strait of Hormuz-linked volatility in crude prices.
